subject: [PATCH v6 00/12] Virtual Swap Space (Swap Table Edition)

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed concerns about locking in the swapoff path, agreeing to restructure in v2 to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap().

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the swap IO path not being able to submit IO for a vswap folio backed by a physical slot, which identifies neither the backing device nor sector. The author modified the code to compute and store the sector from an explicit entry (swap_entry_sector) in various functions, including swap_add_folio, __swap_writeout, and ops->can_merge. This change allows the IO path to address the IO from the stored sector rather than folio->swap.
sentiment_signals: author provided a clear solution to the issue

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing concerns about the reclaim and overcommit logic for vswap, specifically how to handle physical swapfile-less swapping. They acknowledge that anon reclaim gating needs a change to accommodate vswap zswap-backed swapout, and propose adding a new function mem_cgroup_can_swap() to determine whether a cgroup can swap within its headroom. The author also suggests changing the OVERCOMMIT_GUESS heuristic to reference RAM rather than totalram_pages() + total_swap_pages when vswap is enabled.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the swapoff path dropping the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), explaining that dirtying would write uninitialized memory out to swap and instead reports SIGBUS on the next fault.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about the handling of vswap entries in the swap cache, explaining that they are checked under the cluster lock in __swap_cache_add_check() and rejecting a vswap batch if its backing is not THP-amenable. A fix for this issue was already implemented.
reviews.raw_body:
Swap a large anon folio back in as a unit when its vswap entries share a
contiguous run of physical swap slots on a synchronous IO device,
instead of always falling back to order-0 faults.

A zswap-backed or mixed-backing batch is still refused, and the fault
retries at a smaller order.

Signed-off-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>
---
 mm/memory.c     |  5 +++--
 mm/swap_state.c | 17 +++++++++++++----
 mm/zswap.c      |  6 +++++-
 3 files changed, 21 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/memory.c b/mm/memory.c
index 9f651d247eef..430b83900ba8 100644
--- a/mm/memory.c
+++ b/mm/memory.c
@@ -4885,9 +4885,10 @@ static unsigned long thp_swapin_suitable_orders(struct vm_fault *vmf)
 	 * lack handling for such cases, so fallback to swapping in order-0
 	 * folio.
 	 *
-	 * THP swapin for vswap is not supported yet either.
+	 * Vswap entries are checked later, under the cluster lock in
+	 * __swap_cache_add_check().
 	 */
-	if (is_vswap_entry(entry) || !zswap_never_enabled())
+	if (!is_vswap_entry(entry) && !zswap_never_enabled())
 		return 0;
 
 	/*
diff --git a/mm/swap_state.c b/mm/swap_state.c
index 3900975c675f..6c8e8f49e349 100644
--- a/mm/swap_state.c
+++ b/mm/swap_state.c
@@ -174,6 +174,9 @@ static int __swap_cache_add_check(struct swap_cluster_info *ci,
 	unsigned int ci_off, ci_end;
 	unsigned long old_tb;
 	bool is_zero;
+	struct swap_cluster_info_dynamic *ci_dyn;
+	enum vswap_backing_type type;
+	int ret;
 
 	lockdep_assert_held(&ci->lock);
 
@@ -202,11 +205,17 @@ static int __swap_cache_add_check(struct swap_cluster_info *ci,
 		return 0;
 
 	/*
-	 * Reject a vswap batch so __swap_cache_alloc_folio falls back to
-	 * order 0.
+	 * For a vswap entry batch, reject if the backing is not THP-amenable
+	 * (e.g. uniformly ZSWAP, or mixed). The order-fallback loop in
+	 * __swap_cache_alloc_folio will retry with a smaller order on -EBUSY.
 	 */
-	if (is_vswap_entry(targ_entry))
-		return -EBUSY;
+	if (is_vswap_entry(targ_entry)) {
+		ci_dyn = container_of(ci, struct swap_cluster_info_dynamic, ci);
+		ret = __vswap_check_backing(ci_dyn, round_down(ci_off, nr),
+					    nr, &type);
+		if (ret != nr || type == VSWAP_ZSWAP)
+			return -EBUSY;
+	}
 
 	is_zero = __swap_table_test_zero(ci, ci_off);
 	ci_off = round_down(ci_off, nr);
diff --git a/mm/zswap.c b/mm/zswap.c
index 24c4e7a73d56..1b91dba992ab 100644
--- a/mm/zswap.c
+++ b/mm/zswap.c
@@ -1753,9 +1753,13 @@ int zswap_load(struct folio *folio)
 	 * range on the backing device, so scan the range rather than rejecting
 	 * it outright. The caller has pinned every slot, so zswap cannot start
 	 * a store or a writeback into the range while we look.
+	 *
+	 * A vswap batch is checked when the folio enters the swap cache, and
+	 * its backing cannot change after that.
 	 */
 	if (folio_test_large(folio)) {
-		if (WARN_ON_ONCE(zswap_is_present(swp,
+		if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!swap_is_vswap(si) &&
+				 zswap_is_present(swp,
 						  folio_nr_pages(folio)))) {
 			folio_unlock(folio);
 			return -EIO;
-- 
2.53.0-Meta

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about the zswap shrinker skipping vswap entries when out of physical swap space, explained that the mechanism mirrors the existing zswap writeback path but allocates physical backing on demand at writeback time for vswap entries. The author confirmed that this change is correct and will not waste work in case of failure.
sentiment_signals: author confirmed a fix is correct

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that vswap folios can retain physical swapfile space after their swap count reaches zero, agreed to reclaim such slots from the physical reclaim scanner when swap is more than half used (vm_swap_full()) to free physical capacity for new allocations.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about vswap entries being charged against memcg->swap when they don't have physical backing, explaining that this is incorrect and should be changed to charge only when the entry acquires physical backing. The author also refactored swap memcg operations into separate helpers for get, record, charge, uncharge, and put, which will help with charging vswap entries correctly.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about providing additional debugging information for the virtual swap space, and responded by adding two new debugfs counters: 'used' to track allocated pages and 'alloc_reject' to count allocation failures.

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch series introduces Virtual Swap Space, a feature that allows for virtual swap space allocation within the Linux kernel. It enables the use of zswap (a compressed block device) as a backing store for virtual swap space, allowing for more efficient use of physical memory and reducing the need for traditional swap partitions. The patches include various cleanups, bug fixes, and improvements to existing code, including changes to cgroup memory statistics and sysctl parameters. The goal is to provide a flexible and scalable solution for managing swap space in modern Linux systems.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Gregory requested inclusion of disk-swap performance metrics in the patch description, citing a desire for comprehensive comparison with zswap.

Reviewer Gregory questioned why vswap is a boot option instead of a build option, citing no performance impact and suggesting it should be the default.
reviews.raw_body:
I get that the motivation is zswap, but it would be nice to have
disk-swap performance numbers here as well right in the cover.

If only because...

---

If the numbers you presented carry through, I'm left wondering why this
is a boot option and not a build option.  I rather dislike the boot
option compromise in general - but other reasoning aside, if there's no
performance impact, then I don't see why it shouldn't be the default.

~Gregory

-- 
Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
The author acknowledges a performance regression in older versions of the patch, specifically when using zram as a swap backend, and agrees that they closed this gap in their own testing but notes that Kairui did not test the fixed version.

Author acknowledges that bypassing vswap for physical swapfiles was a design decision, and is willing to reconsider it.
reviews.raw_body:
I probably should test it regardless, but likely there will be no
difference in performance numbers. Right now for straight disk
swapping we incur 0 overhead, because I just bypass the virtualization
layer :) There just isn't any feature for me to entertain vswap+disk
swap quite yet (it might come soon-ish though).

Vswap's physical swapfile backend is only used for cgroups that
support zswap (for zswap writeback and fallback if vswap fails to
allocate or zswap rejects the page etc.).

For the older version, I put vswap in front of all swap backends. Disk
swap sees no regression, but Kairui found some regression with fast
in-memory swapfile (pmem). I reproduced it with zram, and I think I
closed that gap in my own testing, but Kairui did not test the fixed
version AFAICT, and I also don't have his full suite, only the ones he
quoted.

(Btw, Kairui, could you publish your full suite, or at least the full
set of testing parameters? I would like to hammer the thing myself to
expose bugs etc.).

---

That's a good point yeah. Lemme think about it. I added the boot param
before I decided to bypass vswap for physical swapfile by default...
